events.asset: DT120 (lysergide tartrate ODT, LSD) Voyage Phase 3 trial (NCT06741228) in generalized anxiety disorder: topline result
events.title: DT120 (LSD) Voyage Phase 3 trial in generalized anxiety disorder reports its topline result
events.proposition: Definium Therapeutics reports the topline primary endpoint result of the Voyage Phase 3 trial (NCT06741228) of DT120 in generalized anxiety disorder (either direction).
events.criterion: TRUE on the date of the first public report of the Voyage trial's primary endpoint result: Definium Therapeutics' topline press release, a results posting on the ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT06741228, or the first peer-reviewed publication that reports the primary result, whichever is first. The result may be positive or negative; the event is about a primary result being reported. An enrollment-complete or last-patient-visit announcement, an interim safety update, a conference abstract without the primary endpoint estimate, or a readout of a different DT120 trial (for example the MDD trial EMERGE) does not count. FALSE at the deadline when no such report is dated by then. Resolution source: Definium Therapeutics' topline press release, with the ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT06741228 as a secondary source.

resolution_source.name: Definium Therapeutics topline press release; ClinicalTrials.gov record NCT06741228 as secondary source

readings: 'Their GAD readout, which is expected later this year' is read as: Definium Therapeutics reports the topline primary result of its GAD Phase 3 program in 2026.
The author names that trial in the same post as Voyage, NCT06741228 (the registry bullet coded at owen-2281), so the event is written on that trial.
The claim is about timing, so the event resolves on the first public report of the primary result in either direction, not on whether the endpoint is met.
'Later this year' = by 31 December 2026 (anchors.json: a year means its last day; origin anchor).
'Readout' = public report of topline primary-endpoint data. An announcement that the trial has completed or that data are in hand, without the result, does not count.

'Is expected' is written in the author's own voice with no source cited, so it is read as his expectation (bin B). A coder who reads it as relayed company guidance would code REPORT; that reading is logged here.

events.asset: Psilocybin, LSD and MDMA drug products: retail-pharmacy dispensing under the FDA-approved labeling or REMS
events.title: Psilocybin, LSD or MDMA drug product approved with retail-pharmacy dispensing
events.proposition: The FDA approves a psilocybin, LSD or MDMA drug product whose approved labeling or REMS permits a retail pharmacy to dispense it to the patient for use outside a healthcare setting.
events.criterion: Resolved on Drugs@FDA (approval letters and approved labeling) read with the FDA REMS database (REMS@FDA). For each drug product whose active ingredient is psilocybin, LSD (lysergide, any salt) or MDMA (midomafetamine, any salt) that the FDA approves between the statement date and the deadline, check the approved labeling and any REMS in force on the approval date. TRUE on the approval date of the first such product whose labeling or REMS permits a retail or community pharmacy to dispense it to the patient or caregiver for use outside a healthcare setting. FALSE at the deadline if at least one such product has been approved and every such approval restricts dispensing to certified healthcare settings or requires administration under healthcare-provider supervision in a healthcare setting. If no such product is approved in the window, the condition is unmet and the item is void.

resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA (approval letters and labeling) with the FDA REMS database (REMS@FDA)

readings: 'Go through a retail pharmacy' reads as the FDA-approved labeling or REMS permitting a retail or community pharmacy to dispense the product to the patient for use outside a healthcare setting.

A product restricted to certified healthcare settings, or whose label requires administration under healthcare-provider supervision in a healthcare setting (the Spravato model the author uses as the reference), does not go through a retail pharmacy.

'Them' and 'these drugs' = drug products whose active ingredient is psilocybin, LSD (lysergide) or MDMA (midomafetamine), in any salt or formulation the sponsor names as such. 'None of them' denies the disjunction, so one event covers all three ('A or B' is one event).

Denial: the forecaster asserts that the proposition is false. The claim presupposes at least one approval; if none occurs in the window, the condition is unmet and the item is void rather than scored as a correct denial.

events.asset: Novel psychedelic drug products: FDA labeling and REMS with no required in-clinic monitoring during or after dosing
events.title: FDA approves a psychedelic drug product with no required post-dose monitoring
events.proposition: The FDA approves a novel psychedelic drug product whose labeling and REMS omit any requirement for in-clinic monitoring of the patient during and after dosing.
events.criterion: Resolved on Drugs@FDA (approval letters and labeling) read with REMS@FDA. A novel psychedelic drug product is the first FDA-approved product with a psychedelic or entactogen active ingredient (the class the forecaster illustrates with psilocybin, LSD and MDMA); ketamine and esketamine products and new formulations of approved drugs do not count. TRUE on the approval date of the first such product, approved after the statement date, whose labeling and REMS require no monitoring of the patient by a healthcare provider during or after dosing (no observation period, no certified-setting dosing requirement). FALSE at the deadline if at least one such product has been approved and every one requires in-clinic monitoring during or after dosing. If none is approved in the window, the condition is unmet and the item is void.

resolution_source.name: Drugs@FDA (approval letters and labeling) with the FDA REMS database (REMS@FDA)
